title: Detroit techno
description: Strings over machines: the Motor City sound, on the skills from the core lessons.
author: Strudel Workshop

tracks.title: Detroit basics
tracks.blurb: Strings, the minor-ninth stab, rolling hats, rimshots and a bass in the gaps, then a groove.

lessons.title: Strings
lessons.goal: Lay a soft, wide string pad under the drums.
lessons.concept:
Detroit techno (Juan Atkins, Derrick May, Kevin Saunderson, mid-1980s) took the drum machine and put **strings** over it: synthesized pads that swell and fade like an orchestra heard from across a lake. The Motor City sound is drums that are hard and strings that are tender.

A **supersaw** is several detuned sawtooths at once, wide and shimmering. A slow **attack** makes each chord fade in; a long **release** lets it hang after the note ends. A **high-pass filter** on the pad keeps its lows out of the kick’s way.

tasks.text: Add a part called strings: a C minor 7 chord on the supersaw, held for the bar, at gain .3.
tasks.hint: const strings = note("[c3,eb3,g3,bb3]").s("supersaw").gain(.3), and stack(kick, clap, strings)

tasks.text: Make it swell: a slow attack of .8 and a release of 1.5.
High-pass the strings at 300 Hz so they stay out of the kick’s way.

challenge.text: Change the chord every two bars: Cm7, then Ab major 7 (ab2 c3 eb3 g3).
challenge.hint: note("<[c3,eb3,g3,bb3]@2 [ab2,c3,eb3,g3]@2>") instead of the fixed chord

summary: Detroit strings: a supersaw chord with slow attack and long release.
High-pass pads so the kick keeps the lows.
@2 inside < > holds an item for two bars.

lessons.title: The Motor City chord
lessons.goal: Stab a minor ninth chord, short and bright.
lessons.concept:
The chord Detroit is known for is the **minor ninth**: a minor seventh with one more note on top (C, E♭, G, B♭, D). It sounds unresolved and a little melancholy, which is the whole mood of the city’s records.

Played as a short **stab** on the offbeats of 2 and 4, it answers the clap. A **square** wave gives it the hollow, plastic edge of the cheap Japanese synths Detroit was made on; a quick **decay** with no **sustain** keeps each hit short.

tasks.text: Add a part called stab: the five notes c3 eb3 g3 bb3 d4 together, on a square wave, hitting on the offbeats of 2 and 4.
tasks.hint: const stab = note("[c3,eb3,g3,bb3,d4]").struct("[~ x]*2").s("square").gain(.4), and stack it

tasks.text: Make every stab short: decay .15 and no sustain.

challenge.text: Put the stab in a room with a short delay: room .3 and a dotted-eighth delay, on its own orbit 2.

summary: The minor ninth is the Detroit chord: m7 plus a ninth on top.
Short stabs on the offbeats of 2 and 4 answer the clap.
A square wave with a fast decay is the classic stab tone.

lessons.title: Rolling 909 hats
lessons.goal: Program 16th hats with accents and open hats on the offbeats.
lessons.concept:
Detroit drums roll. The closed hat runs in **16ths**, never flat: a **gain pattern** puts weight on the beat and lets the in-between hits fall back, so the loop pushes forward. The **open hat** on every offbeat is the "tss" that makes a room move.

The TR-909’s sampled hats are bright and a little metallic, which is exactly the Detroit colour. Two parts, one machine.

tasks.text: Add a part called hats: closed 909 hats on all 16 sixteenths.
tasks.hint: const hats = s("hh*16").bank("RolandTR909"), and stack it

tasks.text: Give the hats a gain pattern so the hit on each beat is the loudest of its four.
Add a part called open: an open hat on every offbeat at gain .45.

challenge.text: Shorten the open hat so it chokes before the next beat.

summary: 16th hats with a gain pattern roll instead of ticking.
Open hats on the offbeats push the groove.

lessons.title: Syncopated rimshots
lessons.goal: Add a rimshot pattern that lands off the grid.
lessons.concept:
Detroit borrowed its percussion feel from funk and electro: short **rimshots** that fall between the kicks instead of on them. That is **syncopation**: accents where you don’t expect them.

A **Euclidean rhythm** spreads hits as evenly as possible across the steps. `"rim(5,16,2)"` puts 5 rimshots across 16 steps, rotated by 2, which lands them off the beat without you placing each one by hand.

tasks.text: Add a part called rim: five 909 rimshots spread over 16 steps with "rim(5,16)".
Rotate it by 2 so the first rimshot leaves the downbeat.

challenge.text: Pan the rimshots to one side and give them a little room.

summary: "x(k,n,rot)" spreads k hits over n steps; the third number rotates.
Pan percussion off-centre; keep kick, bass and clap in the middle.

lessons.title: Bass in the gaps
lessons.goal: Write a filtered bassline that sits between the kicks and in the key.
lessons.concept:
Kick and bass both live in the lows, so Detroit keeps them apart in **time**: the bass plays on the **offbeats**, in the gaps the kick leaves. Each note is short so it never smears into the next kick.

Scale degrees keep it in **C minor** with the strings and the stab: `n("0 5 3").scale("C2:minor")` picks notes of the scale, and the 2 in the scale name puts them in the second octave. A low-pass around 600 Hz rounds the sawtooth off.

tasks.text: Add a part called bass: sawtooth scale degrees of C minor, octave 2, on every offbeat.
tasks.hint: const bass = n("[~ 0] [~ 0] [~ 5] [~ 3]").scale("C2:minor").s("sawtooth"), and stack it

tasks.text: Make every bass note short: decay .15 and no sustain.
Round it off with a low-pass filter at 600 Hz.

challenge.text: Duck the bass under the kick: put the bass on orbit 4 and make the kick duck that orbit.
challenge.hint: .orbit(4) on the bass; .duckorbit(4).duckdepth(.6) on the kick

summary: Offbeat bass leaves the kick its space.
n("…").scale("C2:minor") keeps the bass in key and in octave 2.
Short, filtered notes never smear into the next kick.

lessons.title: Project: a Detroit groove
lessons.goal: Put strings, stab, hats, rimshots and bass together, in one key.
lessons.concept:
All of it in one loop: hard 909 drums, tender strings, a minor-ninth stab, rimshots off the grid and a bass in the gaps. This is the shape of a Transmat or Metroplex 12-inch before the arrangement.

One `const key` keeps the bass in tune with the chords, so moving the whole track to another key is one edit. Keep the strings and the stab quieter than the drums: Detroit mixes let the machines lead.

tasks.text: Add the strings: a C minor 7 supersaw chord with slow attack and release, high-passed, at gain .3.
Add the Motor City stab on the offbeats of 2 and 4, short, on a square wave.
Add rimshots with "rim(5,16,2)" and a bass in the key on the offbeats, short and filtered.
tasks.hint: const rim = s("rim(5,16,2)").bank("RolandTR909").gain(.5) and const bass = n("[~ 0] [~ 0] [~ 5] [~ 3]").scale(key).s("sawtooth").octave(2).decay(.15).sustain(0).lpf(600)

challenge.text: Drop the kick in the last bar of every four, so the strings show through.

summary: A Detroit groove: hard drums, tender strings, a minor-ninth stab, a bass in the gaps.
One const key keeps the bass with the chords.
.mask("<1 1 1 0>") drops a part every fourth bar.
